title: When Knowledge-Tracing Rankings Depend on Available History: A Source-Correction and Matched-Information Audit on ASSISTments 2009 and 2015
abstract: arXiv:2611.32489v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Knowledge-tracing benchmarks often compare models that have different access to a learner's previous responses. We examine how data provenance, history length, and representation affect those comparisons. First, we compare a pinned ASSISTments 2009 sequence mirror against the corrected official release. Of 4,148 learners represented in both, 817 have different ordered skill-response sequences; the mirror also contains fewer labeled events. Second, we retain earlier learner-disjoint model evaluations on the 2009 and 2015 datasets, distinguishing exploratory results from a corrective 2015 replication. Finally, we evaluate a new, nonoverlapping sample of 4,000 ASSISTments 2015 learners using three models constrained to the same one-event or 20-event prior-response window. On 20,592 test responses from 582 learners, the 20-event Brier scores were 0.17667 for count-based logistic regression, 0.17389 for an order-aware logistic model, and 0.17

translated_title: 当知识追踪的排名依赖于可用历史时：对 ASSISTments 2009 与 2015 数据集的数据源修正与信息匹配审计
translated_abstract: 知识追踪基准测试常常在比较对学习者先前作答记录拥有不同访问权限的模型。我们考察数据来源、历史长度以及表示方式如何影响这些比较。首先，我们将一个固定版本的 ASSISTments 2009 序列镜像与修正后的官方发布版本进行对比：在两个数据源中均出现的 4,148 名学习者中，有 817 名学习者的有序技能-作答序列存在差异，且该镜像包含的已标注事件也更少。其次，我们保留了此前在 2009 与 2015 数据集上开展的、按学习者划分互不重叠的模型评估，将探索性结果与针对 2015 数据集的修正性复现区分开来。最后，我们在 4,000 名全新的、互不重叠的 ASSISTments 2015 学习者样本上评估了三个模型，所有模型均被限定使用相同的单次事件或 20 次事件的先前作答窗口。在来自 582 名学习者的 20,592 条测试作答上，20 事件条件下的 Brier 分数分别为：基于计数的逻辑回归 0.17667、顺序感知逻辑模型 0.17389，以及 0.17……
tldr: 该论文通过对 ASSISTments 2009 与 2015 数据集进行数据源修正与信息匹配审计，揭示了知识追踪模型的性能排名依赖于学习者可用历史的长度、来源与表示方式，为公平的模型基准比较提供了重要的方法学依据。
en_tdlr: Through a source-correction and matched-information audit on ASSISTments 2009 and 2015, this paper reveals that knowledge-tracing model rankings depend on the length, provenance, and representation of available learner history, providing key methodological guidance for fair benchmark comparisons.
